etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: A shortening of either obsolete English glibbery (“slippery”) or its source, Low German glibberig, glibberich (“slippery”) / Dutch glibberig (“slippery”).
senses: Having a ready flow of words but lacking thought or understanding; superficial; shallow.
(UK, slang, obsolete) A person's mouth or tongue.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
senses: (historical) A mass of matted hair worn down over the eyes, formerly common in Ireland.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 3
paragraphs: Compare Old English and dialectal English lib (“to castrate, geld”), dialectal Danish live, Low German and Old Dutch lubben.
senses: (obsolete) To castrate; to geld; to emasculate.
